- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.2.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods when sentiment is neutral or mixed; use 1–2 day lag correction for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with true mean; apply mean-reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true if sentiment is “neutral” (0.33–0.67).
